text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: model-runtime-5xx-high-error-rate at 2026-03-15T18:00:00Z - service=model-runner-prod
Maya: I'm oncall, seeing alerts for elevated 5xx across runtime pool A and B. spikes started ~17:52 UTC.
Jordan: grabbing logs now. initial glance shows repeated `segfault` and `killed by OOM` in model-worker processes for model m-redwood-large-v2.
Sam: customer-facing gateway showing 502/504s, some timeouts. We have ~2.3% errors overall, but 10% for a handful of enterprise routes. Tiered routing hasn't kicked in yet.
Maya: @Jordan @Sam please correlate node IDs. I'm invoking the incident playbook: set status to "investigating" and start mitigating for customer impact.
Jordan: tail from node gpu-12:
```
Mar 15 17:50:12 model-runner[2245]: inference: processing request id=abc123 seq=512
Mar 15 17:50:13 model-runner[2245]: runtime: Allocating 1.8GB for kv-cache
Mar 15 17:50:13 model-runner[2245]: runtime: segfault at 0x7ffdeadbeef ip ...
Mar 15 17:50:13 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2245 (model-runner) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 17:50:13 systemd: model-runner.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```
Jordan: stack looks like a memcpy in attention kernel, possibly bad quant kernel on this GPU driver.
Li: any recent rollouts? didn't see infra changes in the last 24h. We did push a model variant yesterday with different custom kernels.
Sam: quick mitigation: scaling down max_batch_size from 256 -> 64 on pool A via runtime-config and enable fallback routing to m-redwood-medium for requests >10s. Applying now.
Maya: doing automated route failover: `redwoodctl routes set --model m-redwood-medium --policy fallback --threshold 0.05`
PagerDuty Bot: Incident acknowledged by Maya (oncall) at 2026-03-15T18:02:10Z
Jordan: I pushed a temporary JVM flag and restarted the model-runner on gpu-12 and gpu-13 to pick up a safer allocator: `--env MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1`. restarting...
Maya: note: enabling node draining on suspect hosts to remove them from rotation: `k8s cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Sam: traffic shifted to fallback model, errors dropped from 2.3% -> 0.9% in 4 minutes. latency for affected routes increased ~200ms but within SLOs. marking customer impact: partial degradation, some increased latency for enterprise routes.
Jordan: found repeated pattern: large sequence requests (seq_len>1024) are allocated into device memory and trigger double-free attempt in quant-kernel. attaching snippet:
```
# backtrace
#0  0x7f5c1a... memcpy
#1  0x7f5c2b... quant_attention::kv_update
#2  0x7f5c3c... model::forward
#3  0x55a4f0 main
```
Jordan: rolling back the custom kernel for the model to the previous stable kernel on pool B. patching now.
Li: notifying support -> sending status update to affected customers and adding a note to the incident.
Maya: good. Sam, can you keep the fallback routing in place until kernel rollback is verified and nodes pass 15m of healthy checks?
Sam: yes, we'll keep fallback for 30m post-rollforward. running health checks: `curl -f http://health-gateway/poolB/ready` in loop.
PagerDuty Bot: Handoff request: Maya -> Jordan at 18:15 UTC if unresolved.
Maya: handing off to Jordan @ 18:15 UTC, I have to step out for a quick call. Jordan, you own next steps and communication.
Jordan: taking over. current mitigation status: fallback routing active, nodes gpu-12/13 drained, kernel rollback in progress on pool B. I'm going to monitor crash rate and memory metrics.
Jordan: rollback applied on 4/5 hosts in pool B, restarting model-runner with `--safe-kernel v1.3.0`.
Sam: metric update: errors down to 0.3% and holding for 6 minutes. no new OOMs detected in the rolled-back hosts.
Li: sending updated customer message: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors due to an unstable inference kernel for large-sequence workloads. We routed traffic to a stable model variant and rolled back the kernel. Root cause investigation continues; a patch will be deployed after validation."
Jordan: will run extended stress on rolled-back nodes: `ab -n 1000 -c 8 -T 'application/json' ...` to simulate large sequences.
Maya: thanks. adding post-incident action items: 1) revert kernel rollout until canary covers large-seq tests; 2) add sequence-length gating in routing to prevent >1024 on unstable kernels; 3) add kdump/gcore capture for future segfault triage.
Jordan: agreed. starting to gather core dumps and enabling extra metrics around allocator and kv-cache sizes.
Sam: I'll keep monitoring; if error rate stays <0.5% for 30m we can de-escalate.
PagerDuty Bot: Status update posted at 2026-03-15T18:28:40Z - Incident severity: high, impact: partial degradation, mitigation: fallback routing + kernel rollback.
Jordan: after 25m post-rollback, no further segfaults and memory stable. planning to reintroduce nodes one at a time and remove fallback after 30m steady state.
Maya: back online, thanks team. I'll write a short timeline for the postmortem.
Li: created customer follow-up draft and assigned to Maya for sign-off.
Sam: closing monitoring loop — keeping alert thresholds slightly tighter for next 48h.
Jordan: final note: root cause likely regression in custom quant attention kernel under large-seq workloads interacting with latest GPU driver; we'll coordinate with runtime-ml to reproduce and harden.
Maya: incident resolved at 2026-03-15T18:36:00Z. :white_check_mark:
